meta.unit: children per woman (tfr); percent (school10, marriage18, age_structure)
meta.release_status: provisional (IIPS NFHS-6 fact sheets, released 29 May 2026; district compendiums released 20-21 Aug 2026 not checked for revisions)

definitions.tfr: total fertility rate: children per woman aged 15-49 at the age-specific rates of the three years before the survey (NFHS-5 report p.111)
definitions.school10: NFHS-6 indicator 12: women age 15-49 with 10 or more years of schooling (%)
definitions.marriage18: NFHS-6 indicator 16: women age 20-24 married before age 18 (%)
definitions.age_structure: NFHS-6 indicators 2 and 3: population below age 15 (%) and age 60 and above (%)

meta.coverage: NFHS-6 gives results for 35 states and union territories (27 states + 8 UTs). Manipur is not in the release (IIPS fact-sheet introduction, p.3, and the IIPS release note). NFHS-5 covered 36 including Manipur. India has 28 states and 8 UTs. The Lok Sabha annexure (S11) lists Manipur with NFHS-5 2.2 and prints NA for NFHS-6.

comparability.rounding: nfhs5 and nfhs6 are the one-decimal figures printed in the NFHS-6 fact sheets. nfhs4 and nfhs3 are the two-decimal values of Table 4.3 of the NFHS-5 India report (identical to the NFHS-4 report) rounded half-up to one decimal; see tfr_report_2dp. Jharkhand NFHS-4 is 2.55, shown 2.6.
comparability.jammu_kashmir_ladakh: NFHS-4 (2015-16) covered one Jammu and Kashmir that included Ladakh (2.01). From NFHS-5 they are separate union territories and the NFHS-5 India report prints na for both in the NFHS-4 column. So Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh have NO nfhs4 in tfr (the old 2.0 was removed on 28 Oct 2026 because it is a different territory); the old-boundary value is kept in tfr_report_2dp as nfhs4_old_boundary and may be shown only with that label.
comparability.dadra_daman_diu: NFHS-4 had Dadra and Nagar Haveli (2.32) and Daman and Diu (1.68) separately; merged in 2020; no combined nfhs4.
comparability.telangana_andhra: Telangana separate from 2014; NFHS-3 (2005-06) has no separate Andhra Pradesh or Telangana TFR in the NFHS-4/5 tables (na).
comparability.tfr_reference_period: each NFHS TFR covers the three years before its survey: about 2013-15 for NFHS-4 and about 2017-19 for NFHS-5 (report table notes); the survey rounds are named 2015-16, 2019-21, 2023-24.
nfhs4_omitted: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

nfhs4_withheld_conflict.Andaman and Nicobar Islands: NFHS-4 TFR is published two ways: 1.5 in the MoHFW/PIB 'Findings of NFHS-4' table of 25 Jul 2017 (S12) and 1.44 (shown 1.4) in Table 4.3 of the NFHS-5 India report (S5). Not settled: the DHS host returned HTTP 403 on the revision pass. So tfr has NO nfhs4 for it. Both are in tfr_report_2dp (nfhs4, nfhs4_pib_2017_1dp). The fall to NFHS-5 (-0.1 or -0.2) is 'about the same' either way.
nfhs4_withheld_conflict.NCT of Delhi: NFHS-4 TFR is 1.7 in the 2017 ministry release (S12) and 1.78 (shown 1.8) in the NFHS-5 report Table 4.3 (S5). Not used in the script; withheld for the same reason.

comparability.nfhs4_checked_against_pib_2017: Every other NFHS-4 value in tfr (Bihar 3.4, Meghalaya 3.0, Assam 2.2, Uttar Pradesh 2.7, Jharkhand 2.6, Nagaland 2.7, Kerala 1.6, Tamil Nadu 1.7, Goa 1.7, Sikkim 1.2, Lakshadweep 1.8, Chhattisgarh 2.2, India 2.2, and all the rest) equals the one-decimal column of the 25 Jul 2017 ministry release (S12); the only differences are the two withheld places. J&K 2.0 and Manipur 2.6 and Dadra and Nagar Haveli / Daman and Diu are in that release but are not in tfr (old boundary, not in NFHS-6, merged).

stats.note_n: 35 = 27 states + 8 union territories with NFHS-6 results (India row excluded; Manipur not in the release)
stats.corr_note: Pearson r across states, each state counts once (not population weighted), printed one-decimal totals; NFHS-5 values are the NFHS-5 column printed in the NFHS-6 fact sheets, same 35 places
stats.lowest_note: ties: after Andaman and Nicobar Islands (0.9) and Sikkim (1.0) and Arunachal Pradesh (1.5), 8 places read 1.6
stats.highest_note: Bihar 2.7; Jharkhand, Lakshadweep, Meghalaya and Uttar Pradesh tie at 2.2; Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan 2.1
stats.biggest_falls_note: Meghalaya -0.7, Andaman and Nicobar Islands -0.4, then four places at -0.3 (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Mizoram)
stats.risers_note: robust = still 0.3 or more after allowing the NFHS-6 one-decimal figure to be off by 0.05 either way against the NFHS-5 report two-decimal figure; Nagaland, Goa and Ladakh are 0.3 on printed figures only

nfhs4_to_nfhs5_incl_manipur.note: NFHS-5 covered 36 places; 33 have an NFHS-4 value in Table 4.3 of the NFHS-5 report (Manipur 2.61 to 2.17 is down); up = Kerala 1.6 to 1.8 and Tamil Nadu 1.7 to 1.8 on one-decimal figures; at two decimals Punjab (1.62 to 1.63) and Tripura (1.68 to 1.70) also tick up
nfhs4_to_nfhs5_incl_manipur.method: Same counts (14 / 14 / 3 / 2) both ways. (a) NFHS-5 report Table 4.3 two-decimal values rounded half-up to one decimal, Manipur 2.61 to 2.17 added. (b) the one-decimal NFHS-4 column of the 25 Jul 2017 ministry release (S12) against the NFHS-5 column of Lok Sabha Q973 (S11), J&K (old boundary), Ladakh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu left out as not comparable. Andaman and Nicobar and Delhi are 'about the same' under either of their NFHS-4 values. Rule: 0.3 or more on the printed figures (editorial, not a significance test).

not_comparable: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

stats.rule: a change is called a rise or a fall only when it is 0.3 or more on the printed one-decimal figures; 0.1 and 0.2 are called about the same (our editorial threshold, not a significance test: IIPS publishes no state-level standard errors in the fact sheets)

lok_sabha_cross_check.note: every NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 state TFR in tfr equals the Lok Sabha annexure

south_west_named_nfhs6.note: the script names these eight states instead of saying 'the south and the west' (no official region definition was read); all read 1.9 or lower. Puducherry 1.6 and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 1.7 are also 1.9 or lower but are not named.
